sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *tuviera* from B1 Unit 4 (*Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría*) and *hubiera* from B1 Unit 35, where *si* + *hubiera* + participle goes with *habría*. A purpose clause can sit inside the result of such a sentence: "If I could, I would do it so that …". The result verb is in the conditional, so the verb of the purpose clause moves to the imperfect subjunctive, the same rule as after a past verb in B1 Unit 38: *Si pudiera, lo haría para que mis hijos estudiaran*. It works with the past conditional too: *Si hubiera podido, lo habría hecho para que no sufrieran*. If the same person acts twice, the purpose is an infinitive as usual: *Si tuviera dinero, viajaría para conocer el mundo*.

sections.title: A purpose in the result clause
rows: Si pudiera, lo haría para que mis hijos estudiaran.
If I could, I would do it so that my children could study.
Si tuviera tiempo, ayudaría a fin de que terminaran antes.
If I had time, I would help so that they would finish sooner.
Si hubiera podido, lo habría hecho para que no sufrieran.
If I had been able to, I would have done it so that they would not suffer.
Si tuviera dinero, viajaría para conocer el mundo.
If I had money, I would travel to see the world. (one person: infinitive)

items.spanish: Si tuviera más dinero, compraría libros para que los niños leyeran más.
items.english: If I had more money, I would buy books so that the children would read more.

items.spanish: Si pudiera, hablaría con ella para que no se sintiera sola.
items.english: If I could, I would talk to her so that she would not feel alone.

items.spanish: Si hubiera tenido tiempo, habría llamado para que supieran que estaba bien.
items.english: If I had had time, I would have called so that they would know I was fine.

items.spanish: Si fuera director, cambiaría el horario a fin de que todos pudieran descansar.
items.english: If I were the director, I would change the schedule so that everyone could rest.

sections.content: Look at the verb before *para que*. If it is a conditional (*haría*, *ayudaría*, *habría hecho*), use the imperfect subjunctive: *para que estudiaran*. If it is a present or a future (*hago*, *haré*), use the present subjunctive: *para que estudien*. Never put a conditional after *para que*: say *para que estudiaran*, not *para que estudiarían*.
